stories.headline: Five oil tankers catch fire in the Strait of Hormuz
body: Iran's forces say five oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in several incidents in the Strait of Hormuz.
One tanker hit a mine, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said.
Iran has sharply limited traffic through the strait, which usually carries a fifth of the world's oil, since the war began in February.
stories.vc: Any threat to Hormuz pushes up oil prices and shipping insurance, which hits India's import bill.

stories.headline: Paraguay's president resigns after a bank collapse, then is impeached
body: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña resigned after the collapse of Ueno Bank froze millions of people's savings.
Minutes later, the lower house voted 78-0 to impeach him.
His own Colorado Party had turned against him amid big protests.
stories.joke: Resigning and getting impeached in one afternoon is efficient, at least.
stories.vc: A digital bank failure toppling a government is a warning on how fast fintech risk can spread.

stories.headline: About 600,000 protest across France over pay and prices
body: Hundreds of thousands of French workers went on strike and marched for higher wages.
About 600,000 people joined nearly 200 protests, the Interior Ministry said; police fired tear gas in some cities.
The Eiffel Tower and Arc de Triomphe were closed.
stories.joke: Even the Eiffel Tower took the day off.
stories.vc: Wage pressure across Europe could keep inflation and interest rates higher for longer.

stories.headline: Sensex soars 2,009 points as oil prices fall
body: The Sensex jumped 2,009 points (2.6%) to about 79,310, and the Nifty closed near 24,537.
Oil prices fell on hopes of a faster end to the West Asia conflict after the US midterms.
Bank and auto shares led the buying.
stories.joke: Oil goes down, Sensex goes up. Rare day the seesaw works for us.
stories.vc: Cheaper oil lowers India's import bill and inflation, which helps companies and the rupee.

stories.headline: Shiprocket turns profitable after listing
body: E-commerce shipping platform Shiprocket made a small ₹0.6 crore profit, against a ₹20.3 crore loss a year ago.
Revenue rose 35% to ₹674 crore.
It listed on the stock market in August.
stories.joke: ₹60 lakh profit: small parcel, big delivery.
stories.vc: Recently listed startups turning profitable supports more Indian tech IPOs.

stories.headline: Karnataka raises bus fares, and commuters are unhappy
body: Karnataka is raising fares on state-run buses.
Commuters say it adds to rising costs, after recent milk and curd price hikes.
Some ask why the state still owes transport corporations money for the free-travel Shakti scheme.
stories.joke: Bengaluru's commute: now pricier, still slow.
stories.vc: Higher fares help cash-strapped bus corporations but may push riders back to private vehicles.

stories.headline: Zipline raises $1.5B as Walmart adds 300 drone sites
body: Drone delivery startup Zipline raised $1.5 billion at a $21.5 billion valuation.
Walmart signed a multi-year deal to add 300 drone delivery sites in the US, up from 21 today.
Investors include Paradigm, Fidelity, Uber and Tiger Global.
stories.joke: Your toothpaste may soon arrive by air.
stories.vc: A retailer of Walmart's size committing to drones makes delivery robotics a serious investment theme.

stories.headline: OpenAI could be ready to go public in 2027, says Brockman
body: OpenAI president Greg Brockman said the company could be ready for an IPO in 2027.
He said OpenAI's sales to businesses are growing fast.
Rival Anthropic has already gained ground in that market.
stories.joke: The race to IPO is now as tight as the race to AGI.
stories.vc: Two AI giants listing within a year would be among the biggest IPO waves ever.

stories.statLabel: minimum order for free Prime delivery
stories.headline: Amazon drops Grubhub and picks Uber Eats for Prime
body: Uber Eats is now Amazon's restaurant delivery partner for US Prime members, replacing Grubhub.
Prime members can order through Amazon without an Uber account.
Delivery is free on orders over $25.
stories.joke: Grubhub, it's not you. Actually, it is.
stories.vc: Access to Prime's huge user base could shift market share in US food delivery towards Uber.

stories.headline: Food startup Wonder files to go public
body: Wonder, founded by Marc Lore, has confidentially filed for an IPO.
It runs food halls where customers order from many restaurant brands at once.
Share numbers and price have not been set.
stories.joke: Food hall today, ticker symbol tomorrow.
stories.vc: Its IPO will test whether investors value food-tech as tech or as restaurants.

stories.headline: Electric truck maker Harbinger raises $240M and moves into defence
body: Harbinger raised a $240 million Series D as it expands into battery storage and defence.
Tiger Global, Capricorn and defence investor Ridgeline led the round.
It has raised over $650 million in total.
stories.joke: Delivery trucks today, military trucks tomorrow.
stories.vc: Climate-tech startups are adding defence work to tap a fast-growing pool of funding.

stories.headline: Nithya Raman set to become Los Angeles' first Asian-American mayor
body: Nithya Raman is projected to beat incumbent Karen Bass to lead Los Angeles.
She will be the city's first Asian-American mayor and second woman elected mayor.
The urban planner focused on housing, affordability and city services.
stories.vc: Her housing focus could reshape how LA spends on homelessness and city building.

stories.headline: Russell Brand convicted of rape and sexual assault
body: A London court convicted Russell Brand of rape and sexual assault involving four women.
The allegations date back more than 20 years.
The judge said he faces a significant prison term and refused him bail before sentencing on Monday.
stories.vc: High-profile convictions push media firms to tighten how they handle abuse complaints.

stories.headline: India's working women doubled, but mostly in low-paid jobs
body: India's female workforce grew from about 104 million in 2017-18 to 201 million in 2025, an ICRIER study says.
Most gains were in farming, self-employment and unpaid family work.
Rural women earn about 45% of what men earn, and unpaid care work keeps many out.
stories.vc: Better-paid jobs for women could add huge value to India's economy; the study links it to trillions by 2047.

stories.headline: Manipal leases land for a 500-bed hospital in Gurugram
body: Manipal Hospitals has leased about 3.5 acres in Gurugram for 30 years to build a multi-speciality hospital.
The first phase will have up to 500 beds.
Delhi NCR is a key growth market for the Bengaluru-based chain.
stories.vc: Big chains leasing land instead of buying it lets them expand faster with less capital.

stories.headline: Medanta approves a ₹997 crore, 500-bed hospital in Ghaziabad
body: Medanta's parent, Global Health, approved ₹997 crore for a new 500-bed hospital in Ghaziabad.
Its quarterly profit rose 38% to ₹219 crore.
The company says it has added about 20% bed capacity so far this year.
stories.vc: Strong profits are funding a bed-building race among India's listed hospital chains.

stories.headline: Apollo plans about 5,800 new beds as profit rises 32%
body: Apollo Hospitals says its expansion is on track to add about 5,800 beds over five years.
Quarterly revenue rose 23% to ₹7,615 crore, and profit rose 32% to ₹630 crore.
Bed occupancy rose to 73% from 69%.
stories.vc: High occupancy gives chains the confidence, and cash, to build more beds.

stories.headline: Mercedes can clinch the constructors' title in Brazil
body: Mercedes will win the 2026 constructors' title if it outscores Ferrari by three points in Brazil.
It has won 12 of 19 races and leads Ferrari, the only team that can catch it, by 126 points.
Kimi Antonelli already won the drivers' title in Mexico.
stories.joke: Ferrari's maths homework: impossible, but due Sunday.
stories.vc: A double title boosts Mercedes' sponsorship value and its share of F1 prize money.
